notes: v2 (26 Sep 2026 review): removed 'reputation'; added a fallback when the default choice is unaffordable; added the 2020Q2 halving to the auction windows; made the negotiation limit direction explicit.

interrupts.trigger: abs(weekly change in BTC or ETH price) >= 15%
interrupts.source: BTC and ETH had many weeks with moves of 15% or more in 2017–22
interrupts.design_note: The weekly series is smoothed (see pack §0), so check with the sim-runner that this fires 1–2 times per volatile quarter. If not, lower to 10%.

choices.label: Curtail for a week and collect credits

interrupts.source: Riot 2022 power credits ≈ $10–30k/MW/month in peak months
interrupts.design_note: Credit must beat forgone revenue or nobody curtails: at 2021 hashprice one MW of S19s earns ~$60k/week, far above the flat $15k/MW. Uri is handled by the uri_2021 card (2.5× forgone revenue).
interrupts.game_note: Structured fields added for the sim (same rules as 'trigger' and 'curtail_credit', review A8). The alert comes at the end of a week in alert_after_week (1-based) and the curtailment is the following week. MW = the Texas machines that would be mining that week. The 'mine' choice's Heat +5 waits for the Heat system.

interrupts.base_fail_note: base_fail = model annual_failure_rate / 52, applied per site; fires when at least 5% of a site's units fail in one week
interrupts.source: Hashboard repair $100–400; fans and PSUs $30–150 (repair-shop price lists, ≈)
Hood County TX and upstate NY noise disputes
interrupts.game_note: Heat design (26 Sep 2026): pay and ignore change the site's grievance, not Heat directly; sound walls share noise mitigation's cost and once-per-site flag (heat.json). One complaint per quarter at most, for the hottest site: rolled once per quarter at a random week, chance (Heat - complaint_chance_offset)%. If the 3-interrupt cap is reached it waits for next quarter.

interrupts.lot: 50–500 used machines of one model at 40–60% of the used price
interrupts.rivals_bid: each of 2–3 rivals bids lot_value * U(0.5, 0.9)
interrupts.source: 2018–19 S9 fire sales; 2020 post-halving S9 dumps; 2022 lender repossessions (Stronghold / NYDIG)
interrupts.game_note: Structured fields added for the sim (same rules as 'trigger', 'lot' and 'rivals_bid'). Models per window follow capital.json 'distressed' (2018–19 S9s and GPU rigs, 2020 post-halving S9s, 2022 S19-class repossessions). Bandwidth from scope §2.6.

interrupts.trigger: crypto_loan.ltv >= 0.70 (warning at 0.65; one week earlier with the Trader hire)

choices.label: Pay the loan down with cash

interrupts.trigger: shocks.json uri: the week before it, if Texas machines would mine that week

choices.label: Curtail during the storm and collect credits

interrupts.game_note: Design thread, 26 Sep 2026: hard-coded (not the uri_2021 event card). Always asked, doesn't count toward the 3 interrupts. Credits as built for curtailment (x curtail_credit_mult: index 1.5). Keep mining: index-contract power x10 that week; fixed contracts unaffected; grievance +5 at Texas as for any 'keep mining'.

interrupts.hidden_limit: opening_offer * U(0.85, 1.15), shifted 5% in the player's favour by the BD Lead (sites) or the Ex-Utility Exec (power)
interrupts.lowball_definition: a counter-offer more than 10% past the hidden limit
interrupts.fallback: accept_offer (used while the mini-game is cut, see scope doc §4)
interrupts.game_note: Design thread, 26 Sep 2026: a power negotiation is a contract RENEWAL. Every non-garage site has a contract; at the end of its term the Plan phase offers a renewal at the site's normal price x opening_mult. Skip = the opening is accepted (terms[0] quarters, 0 BW); negotiate = bw_cost, pick 4 or 8 quarters (8: limit x long_term_limit_mult), then up to 'rounds' counters. The utility's hidden limit = normal price x U(limit_range), NOT the opening. Walking away (either side) = the opening for terms[0] quarters. The fields below replace hidden_limit / lowball_definition above.
